items.stem: From which of the following countries Giuseppe Garibaldi belonged to?
items.answer: Giuseppe Garibaldi was an Italian revolutionary and freedom fighter. In 1860 he led his volunteers, the Red Shirts, into southern Italy and the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, and handed the conquered territory to Victor Emmanuel II. He belonged to Italy.

items.stem:
Match the following and choose the correct option.
(Leader)(Role)
A.Victor Emmanuel II1.Chief Minister of Italy
B.Guiseppe Mazzini2.Young Italy Movement
C.Guiseppe Garibaldi3.Conquered the Kingdom of Sicillies
D.Count Cavour4.Proclaimed as king of Unified Italy
items.answer: Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed king of a unified Italy in 1861, so A matches 4. Mazzini founded the Young Italy movement, so B matches 2. Garibaldi conquered the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, so C matches 3. Cavour was Chief Minister, so D matches 1. The correct pairing is A - 4, B - 2, C - 3, D - 1.

items.stem:
Arrange the following events in chronological order and choose the correct option from the following :
I. Treaty of Constantinople
II. Defeat of Napoleon
III. Unification of Italy
IV. Unification of Germany
items.answer: Napoleon was defeated in 1815, the Treaty of Constantinople recognised Greece in 1832, Italy was unified in 1861 and Germany in 1871. In order the events run II, I, III and IV.
items.ocr: Stem and the roman-numeral list open on p002; the four options and the key are printed at the top of p004.

items.stem: Who among the following was the founder of 'Young Europe' underground secret society in Berne?
items.answer: After being exiled from Italy, Giuseppe Mazzini founded Young Italy in Marseilles and then Young Europe in Berne, a society of like-minded young men from Poland, France, Italy and the German states. The founder was Giuseppe Mazzini.

items.stem: In the above picture of sorrien's utopian vision, the saints, angle and Christ symbolise-
items.answer: In Frederic Sorrieu's 1848 print the peoples of Europe march towards the Statue of Liberty, while above them Christ, the saints and the angels look down from the heavens. That upper register stands for the brotherhood the artist hoped would bind the new nations together, that is, fraternity among nations.
items.ocr: The book prints 'sorrien's' and 'angle'; kept as printed. The painting referred to as 'the above picture' is actually printed directly below the stem.

items.stem:
Assertion (A) : The most serious source of nationalist tension in Europe after 1871 was Balkan.
Reason (R) : A large part of the Balkan was under the control of Ottoman Empire.
items.assertion: The most serious source of nationalist tension in Europe after 1871 was Balkan.
items.reason: A large part of the Balkan was under the control of Ottoman Empire.

options.label: A
options.text: Both, (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both, (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

items.answer: After 1871 the Balkans became the most explosive region in Europe. Much of it lay under a weakening Ottoman Empire, and as Ottoman power receded the Slavic peoples of the region fought one another and drew in the big powers. The Ottoman grip is exactly why the Balkans became the source of tension, so both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion.
items.concept: The Balkans and the road to war

items.stem:
Identify the personality-
• He was an English poet, peer and politician.
• He organised funds and later went to fight in the war.
• He died of fever in 1824.
• He fought on behalf of the Greeks against the Ottoman empire.
items.answer: The English romantic poet Lord Byron raised money for the Greek cause and then joined the fighting himself, dying of fever in Greece in 1824. The personality is Lord Byron.

items.stem: Which of the following was the result of the Act of Union, 1707?

options.label: B
options.text: Unification of the kingdom of Great Britain

items.answer: The Act of Union of 1707 between England and Scotland created the 'United Kingdom of Great Britain', with England holding the dominant partner's share of power. Its result was the unification of the kingdom of Great Britain.

items.stem:
Arrange the following events in the correct sequence and select correct option.
1. Frederic Sorrieu prepared a series of 4 paintings.
2. French Revolution.
3. Napoleon was defeated.
4. Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed the king of united Italy.
items.answer: The French Revolution broke out in 1789, Napoleon was defeated in 1815, Sorrieu made his four prints in 1848 and Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed king of a united Italy in 1861. The sequence is 2, 3, 1, 4.
items.ocr: Stem and options are on p004; the key is printed at the top of p003, which follows p004 in the book (p004 is printed page 29, p003 is printed page 30).

items.stem: Which of the following aspect best signifies this image?

options.label: A
options.text: A map explaining the sea routes used in 18th century by Europeans

options.label: B
options.text: A map celebrating the British Empire.

options.label: C
options.text: A map showcasing the importance of British Empire.

options.label: D
options.text: A map expressing the British ambitions of contouring the world.

items.answer: The print shows a world map with the British possessions coloured in, ringed by the words Freedom, Fraternity and Federation, with Britannia enthroned at the centre and the peoples of the empire bringing their produce to her. It is an imperial celebration, so the image best signifies a map celebrating the British Empire.

items.stem: Which of the following countries were involved in the Three Wars with Prussia and ended with victory and unification of Germany?
items.answer: Between 1864 and 1871 Prussia fought three wars, against Denmark, against Austria and against France. All three ended in Prussian victory, and the last was followed by the proclamation of the German Empire. The countries were Austria, Denmark and France.

items.stem:
Complete the following table with the correct information regarding congress of Vienna.
Name of MeetingHeld in (year)Hosted byMain Objective
Congress of ViennaA - ?B - ?To settle the lost peace in Europe
items.answer: The Congress of Vienna met in 1815, after Napoleon's defeat, and was hosted by the Austrian chancellor Duke Metternich, who drew up the settlement that restored the conservative order in Europe. So A is 1815 and B is the Austrian chancellor duke Metternich.

items.stem:
Study the picture and answer the following question-
Who designed the cover of German almanac?
items.answer: The cover of the German almanac of 1798 was designed by the journalist Andreas Rebmann of Mainz, a member of a Jacobin club, who used the imagery of the guillotine and the fortress to argue for the French revolutionary cause in the German states. The designer was Andreas Rebmann.

items.stem:
Which of the following option(s) is/are correct about Balkan nationalism?
I. The Balkan region became part of the conflict because of the Ottoman Empire.
II. The region comprised of ethnic groups included Greeks, Serbs, Montenegro, etc.
III. British and ethnic nationalities struggled to establish their identity.
Options:
items.answer: The Balkans became a zone of conflict because the Ottoman Empire that held it was breaking up, and the region was inhabited by Slavic ethnic groups such as the Greeks, Serbs, Bulgarians, Montenegrins and Romanians. Statement III is wrong because it was the Slavic, not British, nationalities that struggled for identity. So statements I and II are correct.
items.concept: The Balkans and the road to war
items.ocr: Stem and options are on p003; the key '(a) I & II' is printed at the top of p005.

items.stem:
Assertion (A) : The growth of revolutionary nationalism in Europe sparked off a struggle for independence amongst the Greeks which began in 1821.
Reason (R) : Greece was suffering under subjugation of the Ottoman Empire.
items.assertion: The growth of revolutionary nationalism in Europe sparked off a struggle for independence amongst the Greeks which began in 1821.
items.reason: Greece was suffering under subjugation of the Ottoman Empire.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: C
options.text: A is true but R is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both A and R are false.

items.answer: Greece had been part of the Ottoman Empire since the fifteenth century. The spread of revolutionary nationalism across Europe gave the Greeks both the idea and the support to rise, and the struggle for independence began in 1821. Ottoman subjugation is precisely what the revolt was against, so both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion.

items.stem: Why did the weavers in Silesia revolt against contractors in 1845? Identify the appropriate reason from the following options.

options.label: A
options.text: Contractors did not pay their dues

options.label: B
options.text: Contractors appointed few on high posts

options.label: D
options.text: Contractors gave them loans on high interests

items.answer: The Silesian weavers worked on raw material supplied by contractors who then took the finished cloth. In 1845 the contractors cut payments drastically and failed to settle what they owed, and the desperate weavers marched on the contractor's mansion. The revolt was because the contractors did not pay their dues.

items.stem:
Identify the personality-
• Two female allegories of France and German.
• They stood as personifications of the 'Republic' and 'Liberty'.
• These allegories remind the public of the national symbol of unity and to persuade them to identify with it.
• They were portrayed that they game the abstract idea of a nation in a concrete form.
items.answer: France was personified as Marianne, who carried the attributes of the Republic and of Liberty, and the German nation was personified as Germania. Together these two female allegories gave the abstract idea of the nation a visible form. The pair is Marianne and Germania.
items.ocr: The book prints 'they game the abstract idea'; kept as printed.

items.stem: Which of the following treaty recognized Greece as an independent nation?
items.answer: The Greek war of independence, begun in 1821 and supported by west European sympathisers as well as by Russia, ended when the Treaty of Constantinople of 1832 recognised Greece as an independent nation.

Each letter dropping out of Napoleon's bag bears-

options.label: B
options.text: The names of the territories he conquered.

options.label: D

items.answer: The caricature shows Napoleon in retreat, striding away while sheets bearing place names spill out of the basket on his back. Those sheets are the lands slipping from his grasp, so each letter bears the names of the territories he lost.

items.stem: Which one of the following was not included in the 'Napoleonic Code' of 1804 ?
items.answer: The Civil Code of 1804 did away with all privileges based on birth, established equality before the law and secured the right to property. Since it abolished birth privilege rather than including it, the answer is privilege based on birth.

items.stem: Identify the correct statement with regard to the 'Zollverein' from the following options:

options.label: A
options.text: It was a coalition of Prussian states formed to manage political alliances.

options.label: B
options.text: Its aim was to bind the Prussia politically into an association.

options.label: C
options.text: It was a Custom Union at the initiative of Prussia.

options.label: D
options.text: It helped to awaken and raise national sentiment in Europe.

items.answer: The Zollverein of 1834 was a customs union formed at Prussia's initiative. It abolished tolls between the member German states and reduced the number of currencies, binding them economically well before they were bound politically. It was a Custom Union at the initiative of Prussia.
items.ocr: Stem and option (a) are at the foot of p005; options (b) to (d) and the key are at the top of p006.

items.stem:
Assertion (A) : In Britain the formation of the nation-state was not the result of a sudden upheaval or revolution.
Reason (R) : The first clear expression of nationalism came with the French Revolution in 1789.
items.assertion: In Britain the formation of the nation-state was not the result of a sudden upheaval or revolution.
items.reason: The first clear expression of nationalism came with the French Revolution in 1789.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: C
options.text: A is true but R is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both A and R are false.

items.answer: The British nation-state was built up slowly over many centuries, by the Act of Union with Scotland in 1707 and the incorporation of Ireland in 1801, and not by any single revolution. It is also true that the first clear expression of nationalism came with the French Revolution of 1789, but that fact concerns France and does not explain the gradual British case. Both statements are true and the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

items.stem: Identify the ideology under which people demanded freedom of markets in early-nineteenth-century Europe.
items.answer: For the commercial classes of early nineteenth century Europe liberalism meant freedom of markets and the abolition of state-imposed restrictions on the movement of goods and capital, alongside equality before the law. The ideology is liberalism.

items.stem:
Arrange the following events in the correct sequence and select correct option.
1. Fall of Napoleon.
2. Napoleon invades Italy.
3. The defeat of Napoleon by Britain, Russia.
4. Napoleon lost the battle of Leipzig.
items.answer: Napoleon invaded Italy in 1797, lost the battle of Leipzig in 1813, fell from power in 1814 and was finally defeated by the allied powers at Waterloo in 1815. The sequence is 2, 4, 1, 3.

items.stem: Proclaimed German Emperor in a ceremony held at Versailles.
items.answer: In January 1871 the Prussian king William I was proclaimed German Emperor in a ceremony held in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, attended by the princes of the German states and by Bismarck and the army. The answer is William I.

items.stem: Which among the following best signifies the idea of liberal nationalism of nineteenth century Europe ?

options.label: C
options.text: Freedom for individual and equality before law

items.answer: Liberal nationalism in nineteenth century Europe stood for government by consent, an end to privileges of birth, the inviolability of private property and, above all, freedom for the individual and equality of all before the law.
items.ocr: CONTRADICTED KEY. The book prints 'Ans : (d) Supremacy of State oriented nationalism.' but the same question is reprinted as Q50 on p010 with the key '(c) Freedom for individual and equality before law'. Option (d) is the opposite of liberal nationalism, so the solution wins and the key is recorded here as (c).

items.stem:
Assertion (A) : Serfdom and bonded labour were abolished in Habsburg dominion and Russia.
Reason (R) : Monarchs had realised that revolution could be resisted only by granting concessions to liberal nationalist rebels.
items.assertion: Serfdom and bonded labour were abolished in Habsburg dominion and Russia.
items.reason: Monarchs had realised that revolution could be resisted only by granting concessions to liberal nationalist rebels.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: C
options.text: A is true but R is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both A and R are false.

items.answer: In the years after 1848 the Habsburg rulers and the Russian tsar abolished serfdom and bonded labour. They did so because the wave of revolutions had shown the monarchs that the cycle of revolt could only be broken by conceding some of what the liberal nationalists demanded. Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion.

items.stem: Which of the following revolutions is called as the first expression of nationalism?
items.answer: The French Revolution of 1789 transferred sovereignty from the monarchy to a body of French citizens and created a set of measures, a new flag, a common language, a single system of weights and measures, that made the French a nation. It is called the first clear expression of nationalism.

items.stem:
Consider these statements about the Image given below
1. Title of this caricature is “The Club of Thinkers”.
2. he plaque on the left bears the inscription: 'The most important question of today's meeting: How long will thinking be allowed to us?'
3. This was a caricature of meeting called by liberals.
4. This caricature was created in 1820.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
items.answer: The caricature is titled 'The Club of Thinkers', the plaque carries the question about how long thinking will be allowed, and it dates from about 1820, when the Karlsbad decrees imposed censorship. It mocks the censorship of the conservative order rather than depicting a liberal meeting, so statement 3 is wrong and statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct.
items.ocr: Statement 2 is printed with a dropped capital as 'he plaque'; kept as printed. Option (a) is printed as 'A. 1 only'; kept as printed.

items.stem: “When France sneezes, the rest of Europe catches cold”. Who among the following said this popular line?
items.answer: The Austrian chancellor Metternich made this remark about the July Revolution of 1830 in France, meaning that political upheaval in France was always followed by upheaval elsewhere in Europe. The line is Metternich's.
items.ocr: The book spells option (b) 'Matternich' (Metternich); kept as printed.

items.stem: Which of the following is not a part of the 'United Kingdom of Great Britain' ?
items.answer: The United Kingdom of Great Britain was formed by the Act of Union of 1707 between England and Scotland, and it included Wales. Ireland was brought in only later, by the Act of Union of 1801, which produced the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland. So Ireland is not a part of the United Kingdom of Great Britain.
items.ocr: Option (b) Poland is also literally not a part of Great Britain, so the question has two defensible answers; the intended distractor set is about the British Isles and the printed key (d) Ireland is kept.

items.stem: Identify the correct statement with regard to 'The Act of Union -1707' from the following options.

options.label: A
options.text: The British monarchy surrendered the power to English Parliament.

options.label: B
options.text: The British parliament seized power from Ireland.

options.label: C
options.text: The formation of the 'United Kingdom of Great Britain'.

options.label: D
options.text: The British nation was formed as a result of a war with Scotland and Wales.

items.answer: The Act of Union of 1707 joined England and Scotland and brought into being the 'United Kingdom of Great Britain'. It was an act of union, not a conquest, so the correct statement is the formation of the 'United Kingdom of Great Britain'.
items.ocr: Stem and options are at the foot of p007; the key is printed at the top of p008.

items.stem: Who among the following was proclaimed as the 'German Emperor' in 1871 ?
items.answer: On 18 January 1871 the Prussian king William I was proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, completing the unification of Germany. The answer is William I.

Column AColumn B

BKing Victor Emmanuel II2.Revolutionary who tried to unify Italy

DGiuseppe Garibaldi4.Through a tactful diplomatic alliance with France he succeeded in defeating the Austrian forces in 1859
items.answer: Mazzini was the revolutionary who tried to unify Italy, so A matches 2. Victor Emmanuel II was the ruler of an Italian princely house, Sardinia-Piedmont, so B matches 1. Cavour engineered the alliance with France that defeated Austria in 1859, so C matches 4. Garibaldi led the volunteers towards Rome and the Papal States, so D matches 3. The correct pairing is A - 2, B - 1, C - 4, D - 3.

items.stem:
Assertion (A) : The issue of extending political rights to women was a controversial one within the liberal movement.
Reason (R) : Women were considered more superior and independent of men by the society, because of their enthusiastic performance in liberal movement.
items.assertion: The issue of extending political rights to women was a controversial one within the liberal movement.
items.reason: Women were considered more superior and independent of men by the society, because of their enthusiastic performance in liberal movement.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: C
options.text: A is true but R is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both A and R are false.

items.answer: Women took an active part in the liberal movement, founding political associations and newspapers, yet when the Frankfurt Parliament met they were admitted only as observers in the visitors' gallery, and the question of votes for women split the liberals. So the assertion is true. The reason is false: society did not treat women as superior to or independent of men. Hence A is true but R is false.

items.stem: Why was Otto von Bismarck considered as the chief architect of German unification ? Choose the correct option from the following:

options.label: A
options.text: He allianced with Italy and France for the unification process.

options.label: B
options.text: He granted autonomy to Prussia with Conservatives.

options.label: C
options.text: He carried the nation-building process with the army and the bureaucracy.

options.label: D
options.text: He carried Libera list and Romantic scholars for cultural movement.

items.answer: After 1848 the leadership of German unification passed from the liberals to Prussia, and its chief minister Otto von Bismarck drove the process through with the Prussian army and bureaucracy, winning three wars in seven years. He is called the chief architect of German unification because he carried the nation-building process with the army and the bureaucracy.
items.ocr: CONTRADICTED KEY. The book prints 'Ans : (b) He granted autonomy to Prussia with Conservatives.', which is not a meaningful account of Bismarck's role; option (c) is the textbook account of Prussian nation-building through the army and the bureaucracy, so the solution wins and the key is recorded as (c). The question number is partly hidden behind the vertical NODIA watermark but is 38 by sequence.

items.stem: Choose the correct statement about the image given bellow.

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C

items.answer: The print shows Germania lying fallen on the ground beside a skull, an image made after the defeat of the liberal revolution. It is 'The Fallen Germania' by Julius Hübner. 'Germania Guarding the Rhine' is a different painting, by Lorenz Clasen. So the correct statement is that the image was painted by Julius Hübner.

items.stem: Who among the following leaders formed a secret society called 'Young Italy' ?
items.answer: Giuseppe Mazzini, exiled for his part in a Carbonari rising in Liguria, founded the secret society Young Italy in Marseilles, and later Young Europe in Berne. The leader is Giuseppe Mazzini.

items.stem:
Arrange the following events related to the formation of nation-state of Britain in chronological order :
I. Act of Union between England and Scotland.
II. English Parliament seized power from Monarchy.
III. Ireland was forcibly incorporated into the United Kingdom.
IV. Catholic revolt against British dominance.
Options :
items.answer: The English Parliament seized power from the monarchy in the Glorious Revolution of 1688, the Act of Union with Scotland followed in 1707, Wolfe Tone's Catholic-backed revolt against British dominance was crushed in 1798, and Ireland was forcibly incorporated into the United Kingdom in 1801. The order is II – I – IV – III.

items.stem:
Identify the personality-
• He was a French philosopher.
• He insisted on social capital.
• According to him, nations are not formed by common language, race and religion.
• According to him liberty would be lost if there was only one law and only one master.
items.answer: The clues describe the French philosopher Ernest Renan, who argued in 'What is a Nation?' that a nation is not made by race, language or religion but by a shared heritage and a daily plebiscite of consent, and who warned that liberty would be lost if there were only one law and only one master. The personality is Renan.
items.ocr: CONTRADICTED KEY. The book prints 'Ans : (d) Carbonari', but the Carbonari were an Italian secret society, not a French philosopher, and every clue in the stem is Ernest Renan, whom the chapter's own glossary on p002 lists as 'a great French philosopher'. The solution wins and the key is recorded as (a) Renan.

items.stem: Which of the following was NOT visualised by Frederic Sorrieu in his first print of series of four prints made up of 'Democratic and social republic' ?

options.label: A
options.text: The people of America and Europe men and women of all ages.

options.label: B
options.text: Social classes marching on a long train

options.label: C
options.text: Offering homage to the statue of unity.

items.answer: In Sorrieu's first print the peoples of America and Europe, men and women of all ages and social classes, march in a long train to offer homage to the Statue of Liberty. The statue in the print is Liberty, not unity, so offering homage to the statue of unity was not visualised.
items.ocr: The stem begins at the foot of the left column of p009 and is completed at the top of the right column of the same page.

items.stem: The postage stamp shows the female allegory - Marianne. Which country does she represents?
items.answer: Marianne is the female allegory of the French Republic, and the stamp is inscribed 'REPUB. FRANC.' with the value in centimes. She represents France.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements is true about nation-states?

options.label: A
options.text: Citizens share a common sense of shared identity or history.

options.label: B
options.text: Nation-state is a state ruled by one absolute ruler.

options.label: C
options.text: Commonness is forged through linguistic factor only

options.label: D
options.text: Nation-states are directly ruled by the people and based on heterogenization of society.

items.answer: A nation-state is one in which the majority of the citizens, and not only its rulers, come to develop a sense of common identity and shared history. That commonness is forged through struggles and shared experience, not through language alone or through absolute rule. The true statement is that citizens share a common sense of shared identity or history.

items.stem:
Assertion (A) : King Victor Emmanuel II tried to unify the Italian states through war.
Reason (R) : In the eyes of the ruling elites of this region, a unified Italy offered them the possibility of economic development and political dominance.
items.assertion: King Victor Emmanuel II tried to unify the Italian states through war.
items.reason: In the eyes of the ruling elites of this region, a unified Italy offered them the possibility of economic development and political dominance.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: C
options.text: A is true but R is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both A and R are false.

items.answer: Sardinia-Piedmont under Victor Emmanuel II led the wars that unified Italy. The ruling elites of the region backed that policy because a unified Italy promised them economic development and political dominance, which is exactly why the king pursued unification by war. Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion.

items.stem: Select the correct definition to define the term 'Plebiscite'.

options.label: A
options.text: Plebiscite is a direct vote by which only the female members of a region are asked to accept or reject a proposal.

options.label: B
options.text: Plebiscite is a direct vote by the male members of a region are asked to accept or reject a proposal.

options.label: C
options.text: Plebiscite is a direct vote by only a chosen few from the total population of a particular region to accept or reject a proposal.

options.label: D
options.text: Plebiscite is a direct vote by which all the citizens of a region are asked to accept or reject a proposal.

items.answer: A plebiscite is a direct vote put to the whole electorate of a region, as in Nice and Savoy in 1860, and not to any restricted group. It is a direct vote by which all the citizens of a region are asked to accept or reject a proposal.

items.stem:
Identify the class
• They owned states in the countryside and also town houses.
• They spoke French for purposes of diplomacy and in high society.
• Their families were often connected by ties of marriage.
items.answer: The landed aristocracy of Europe owned estates in the countryside and town houses as well, used French for diplomacy and in high society, and were bound together across countries by ties of marriage. The class is the aristocrats.
items.ocr: The book prints 'They owned states' for 'estates'; kept as printed.

items.stem: Which among the following best signifies the idea of liberal nationalism of nineteenth century Europe?

options.label: C
options.text: Freedom for individual and equality before law

items.answer: Liberalism in nineteenth century Europe stood for government by consent, the end of privileges based on birth and, at its core, freedom for the individual and equality of all before the law.
items.ocr: This is the same question as Q28 on p007, where the book prints the key as (d); here it prints (c), which is the correct answer.

items.stem:
Arrange the following events in the correct sequence and select correct option.
1. Unification of Germany.
2. Acts of Union.
3. Unification of Italy.
4. Vienna Peace Settlement.
items.answer: The Acts of Union were passed in 1707, the Vienna Peace Settlement was made in 1815, Italy was unified in 1861 and Germany in 1871. The sequence is 2, 4, 3, 1.

items.stem: Which of the following was not the objective of Treaty of Vienna 1815 ?

options.label: A
options.text: The Bourbon dynasty was restored to power.

options.label: B
options.text: France lost the territories it had annexed under Napoleon.

options.label: C
options.text: A series of states were set up on the boundaries of France to prevent French expansion in future.

options.label: D
options.text: The main intention was to restore the liberal democratic order that had been overthrown by Napoleon.

items.answer: The Vienna settlement of 1815 restored the Bourbon dynasty, stripped France of the territories Napoleon had annexed and ringed France with a belt of states to block future expansion. Its purpose was to restore the conservative monarchical order, not a liberal democratic one, so option (d) was not an objective.
items.ocr: Stem is at the foot of p010; the four options and the key are at the top of p011.

items.stem: Who is shown in this picture sitting on knees?
items.answer: The cartoon shows Garibaldi in his rough campaign dress kneeling to pull the boot marked ITALY on to the foot of the crowned Victor Emmanuel II, the gesture by which he handed over his southern conquests to the king. The kneeling figure is Giuseppe Garibaldi.

items.stem:
Match column A and column B and choose the correct option.
Column AColumn B
A.Absolutist1.A vision of society
B.Utopian2.A form of government
C.Plebiscite3.A system of direct vote
D.Suffrage4.A system of holding election
items.answer: Absolutism is a form of government in which power is centralised and unrestrained, so A matches 2. A utopia is a vision of a society so ideal that it is unlikely to exist, so B matches 1. A plebiscite is a system of direct vote, so C matches 3. Suffrage is the system of holding elections and the right to vote in them, so D matches 4. The correct pairing is A - 2, B - 1, C - 3, D - 4.

items.stem: What were the consequences of the July revolution of 1830 ?

options.label: A
options.text: A constitutional monarchy with Louis Philippe at its head was installed in France

options.label: B
options.text: Uprising in Brussels took place which led to Belgium breaking away from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands

items.answer: The July Revolution of 1830 drove out the Bourbon king and installed a constitutional monarchy under Louis Philippe, and the shock of it set off the uprising in Brussels that took Belgium out of the United Kingdom of the Netherlands. Both consequences followed, so the answer is both a and b.

items.stem:
Identify the group of people who had -
• Commitment to oppose monarchical forms that had been established after the Vienna Congress
• Willingness to to fight for liberty and freedom.
• They saw the creation of nation-states as a necessary part of this struggle for freedom.
items.answer: After 1815 secret societies sprang up across Europe of men committed to opposing the monarchical order restored by the Congress of Vienna, ready to fight for liberty and freedom, and convinced that nation-states had to be created for that freedom to be won. Such people were called revolutionaries.
items.ocr: The book prints 'Willingness to to fight'; kept as printed.

items.stem: Which among the following was the main reasons for the weavers to revolt against contractors in Silesia, in 1845?

options.label: B
options.text: They stopped the supply of the raw material to them.

options.label: C
options.text: They refuse to place orders for finished textiles.

options.label: D
options.text: It was the wave of revolution.

items.answer: The Silesian weavers depended on contractors who supplied the raw material and took the finished cloth. In 1845 the contractors cut the payments drastically, and the weavers, reduced to destitution, marched in pairs on the contractor's mansion and ransacked it. The main reason was that the contractors reduced their payments drastically.
